I'm thinking of buying a new laptop and I don't know if I should avoid getting one with a AMD GPU. I'm not into gaming and such, I just need it to play HD video and browse the web. Is it going to be a hassle? Am I going to have constant screen tearing?
What is the current state of AMD graphics on Linux?
Likely it will work but not be as good as an nvidia based system in games.

The open source drivers are plenty for what you are looking for. They are part of the kernel so no special installation is required.

The only real problem with AMD on Linux is when it comes to gaming. Open source drivers aren't up to nvidia's level and even the proprietary drivers aren't that great.

But, if all you care about is watching videos and surfing the web, you won't have any problems.

Both the open source and Catalyst have been improving greatly over the years, but Catalyst still isn't as good as Nvidia's proprietary drivers. The last time I used Nvidia their open source drivers were complete garbage. Don't know what's the situation now with them, but AMD's open source drivers are really good and they keep improving greatly.

If you're not into gaming though, AMD drivers are completely fine. The issues begin with gaming because all the games that I've played on AMD are playable with decent framerates, but Nvidia always gives more performance in the same price range, so if you can live with that go AMD.

EDIT

Also, about screen tearing, the Catalyst drivers come with the Tear Free option in settings so you won't have such issues.
Having a tear free option doesn't mean it works! (It usually does, but there have been some cases where it very very clearly did not.)
Well, I spoke from my experience. I never had screen tearing with the option enabled. Not in video games, movies or anything. It could happen I suppose, I don't know.

In short: Nvidia proprietary drivers > AMD Catalyst (proprietary) > AMD opensource > Nvidia opensource.

If you don't game, you're with everything (except maybe Nvidia opensource), if you would game, then using proprietary drivers is kinda a must (and yes, Nvidia will squeeze more performance on Linux, however that might change with DX12 games).

Edit: I have both AMD (desktop) and Nvidia (notebook, not used much). With AMD (even with open drivers) you won't really ahve any screen tearing, so don't worry about that.
